items.stem: What is meant by a homologous series?
options: compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen
compounds with the same molecular formula
compounds with the same boiling point
a family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula, each member differing by CH₂
items.answer: a family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula, each member differing by CH₂
items.markingKey: Similar chemical properties; gradual change in physical properties.

items.stem: Explain why members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties.
items.answer: They contain the same functional group, which determines how the molecules react.
items.markingKey: same functional group [1]; functional group determines reactions [1]

items.stem: Explain why the boiling points of the alkanes increase with chain length.
items.answer: Longer molecules have more electrons and larger surface area, so stronger instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces.
items.markingKey: more electrons/surface contact [1]; stronger London forces [1]

items.stem: For 2-methylpropan-2-ol, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula.
items.answer: (a) (CH₃)₃COH (b) C₄H₁₀O (c) C₄H₁₀O
items.markingKey: (a) (CH₃)₃COH [1]; (b) C₄H₁₀O [1]; (c) C₄H₁₀O [1]

items.stem: For methylamine, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula.
items.answer: (a) CH₃NH₂ (b) CH₅N (c) CH₅N
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃NH₂ [1]; (b) CH₅N [1]; (c) CH₅N [1]

items.stem: For 2-methylpropanoic acid, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula. Name the homologous series and identify the functional group.
items.answer: (a) (CH₃)₂CHCOOH (b) C₄H₈O₂ (c) C₂H₄O; carboxylic acid: –COOH
items.markingKey: (a) (CH₃)₂CHCOOH [1]; (b) C₄H₈O₂ [1]; (c) C₂H₄O [1]; carboxylic acid, –COOH [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Dhaka analyses three compounds: HCOOCH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂CHO, CH₃CH₂NH₂. (a) Name compound A (HCOOCH₂CH₃) and identify its homologous series. (b) Name compound B (CH₃CH₂CHO) and identify its homologous series.
items.answer: (a) ethyl methanoate; ester (b) propanal; aldehyde
items.markingKey: (a) ethyl methanoate; ester [2] (b) propanal; aldehyde [2]

items.stem: Leila is given three compounds in a school laboratory: (CH₃)₂CHCOOH, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃. (a) Name compound B (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) and identify its homologous series. (b) Name compound C (CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃) and identify its homologous series. (c) Define the term functional group.
items.answer: (a) propan-1-ol; alcohol (b) 2-methylbutane; alkane (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
items.markingKey: (a) propan-1-ol; alcohol [2] (b) 2-methylbutane; alkane [2] (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound. [1]

items.stem: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
items.answer: CₙH₂ₙ
items.markingKey: Alkenes (one C=C): CₙH₂ₙ; alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items.stem: To which homologous series does CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ belong?
items.answer: alcohol
items.markingKey: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ (propan-2-ol) contains –OH (hydroxyl): alcohol.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a displayed formula and a structural formula.
items.answer: A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond; a structural formula shows the arrangement of atoms in each carbon unit without showing all bonds (e.g. CH₃CH₂OH).
items.markingKey: displayed shows all bonds [1]; structural shows groupings without bonds [1]

items.stem: A student in Toronto claims that the longest chain in CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ has three carbons, so it is propane. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. The longest chain is three carbons, but there is also a methyl branch on C2, so the compound has 4 carbons: 2-methylpropane (C₄H₁₀).
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: For 2-methylpropanal, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula.
items.answer: (a) (CH₃)₂CHCHO (b) C₄H₈O (c) C₄H₈O
items.markingKey: (a) (CH₃)₂CHCHO [1]; (b) C₄H₈O [1]; (c) C₄H₈O [1]

items.stem: For methanol, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula.
items.answer: (a) CH₃OH (b) CH₄O (c) CH₄O
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃OH [1]; (b) CH₄O [1]; (c) CH₄O [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Accra analyses three compounds: CH₃COOCH₃, CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃. (a) Give the molecular formula of each compound. (b) Draw the displayed formula of the first compound.
items.answer: (a) C₃H₆O₂; C₄H₁₀; C₄H₈O₂ (b) All atoms and bonds of CH₃COOCH₃ shown.
items.markingKey: (a) C₃H₆O₂; C₄H₁₀; C₄H₈O₂ [2] (b) All atoms and bonds of CH₃COOCH₃ shown. [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Kuala Lumpur analyses three compounds: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH, (CH₃)₂CHCOOH, HCOOCH₂CH₃. (a) Name compound A (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH) and identify its homologous series. (b) Name compound B ((CH₃)₂CHCOOH) and identify its homologous series. (c) Define the term functional group.
items.answer: (a) butan-1-ol; alcohol (b) 2-methylpropanoic acid; carboxylic acid (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
items.markingKey: (a) butan-1-ol; alcohol [2] (b) 2-methylpropanoic acid; carboxylic acid [2] (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound. [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Madrid analyses three compounds: CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl, CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂, HCHO. (a) Name compound A (CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl) and identify its homologous series. (b) Name compound B (CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂) and identify its homologous series. (c) Give the molecular formula of each compound.
items.answer: (a) 1-chloropropane; halogenoalkane (b) propylamine; amine (c) C₃H₇Cl; C₃H₉N; CH₂O
items.markingKey: (a) 1-chloropropane; halogenoalkane [2] (b) propylamine; amine [2] (c) C₃H₇Cl; C₃H₉N; CH₂O [2]

items.stem: What is homolytic fission?
options: breaking a covalent bond so that each atom takes one electron, forming two free radicals
forming a bond using a lone pair
breaking a bond so that one atom takes both electrons
items.answer: breaking a covalent bond so that each atom takes one electron, forming two free radicals
items.markingKey: e.g. Cl₂ → 2Cl• in UV light.

items.stem: Explain why OH⁻ ions attack the carbon atom of the C–Br bond in bromoethane.
items.answer: Br is more electronegative so C is δ+; OH⁻ is a nucleophile that donates a lone pair to the electron-deficient carbon.
items.markingKey: C δ+ [1]; OH⁻ donates lone pair (nucleophile) [1]

items.stem: Explain why alkenes react with electrophiles rather than nucleophiles.
items.answer: The C=C π bond is a region of high electron density that attracts electron-pair acceptors (electrophiles) and repels nucleophiles.
items.markingKey: high electron density in π bond [1]; attracts electrophiles [1]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: Cl•; CN⁻; a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃.
items.answer: Cl•: free radical; CN⁻: nucleophile; a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃: electrophile
items.markingKey: Cl• free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] CN⁻ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃ electrophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃; Cl•; CN⁻.
items.answer: a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃: electrophile; Cl•: free radical; CN⁻: nucleophile
items.markingKey: a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃ electrophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] Cl• free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] CN⁻ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: Grace compares the mechanisms of three reactions: methane with chlorine in UV light, ethene with bromine, and bromoethane with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide. (a) Name the mechanism of each reaction. (b) State what is shown by a curly arrow.
items.answer: (a) free-radical substitution; electrophilic addition; nucleophilic substitution (b) Movement of a pair of electrons.
items.markingKey: (a) free-radical substitution; electrophilic addition; nucleophilic substitution [3] (b) Movement of a pair of electrons. [1]

items.stem: What is heterolytic fission?
options: breaking a covalent bond so that one atom takes both bonding electrons, forming ions
items.answer: breaking a covalent bond so that one atom takes both bonding electrons, forming ions
items.markingKey: e.g. C–Br → C⁺ + Br⁻.

items.stem: Explain why UV light is needed for the reaction of methane with chlorine.
items.answer: UV provides energy for homolytic fission of the Cl–Cl bond to form chlorine radicals that start the chain reaction.
items.markingKey: homolytic fission of Cl₂ [1]; radicals initiate chain [1]

items.stem: A student in Kathmandu claims that in homolytic fission the more electronegative atom takes both electrons. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. That is heterolytic fission; in homolytic fission each atom takes one electron.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: •CH₃; NH₃; H⁺.
items.answer: •CH₃: free radical; NH₃: nucleophile; H⁺: electrophile
items.markingKey: •CH₃ free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] NH₃ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] H⁺ electrophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: NH₃; Br₂ (polarised by the C=C); •CH₃.
items.answer: NH₃: nucleophile; Br₂ (polarised by the C=C): electrophile; •CH₃: free radical
items.markingKey: NH₃ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] Br₂ (polarised by the C=C) electrophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] •CH₃ free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: Freya compares the mechanisms of three reactions: methane with chlorine in UV light, ethene with bromine, and bromoethane with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide. (a) Identify the attacking species in the reaction of bromoethane with OH⁻ and explain why it attacks carbon. (b) State what is shown by a curly arrow.
items.answer: (a) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative. (b) Movement of a pair of electrons.
items.markingKey: (a) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative. [2] (b) Movement of a pair of electrons. [1]

items.stem: Felix compares the mechanisms of three reactions: methane with chlorine in UV light, ethene with bromine, and bromoethane with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide. (a) Define homolytic and heterolytic fission. (b) Identify the attacking species in the reaction of bromoethane with OH⁻ and explain why it attacks carbon.
items.answer: (a) Homolytic: each atom takes one electron (radicals); heterolytic: one atom takes both (ions). (b) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative.
items.markingKey: (a) Homolytic: each atom takes one electron (radicals); heterolytic: one atom takes both (ions). [2] (b) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative. [2]

items.stem: What is the H–C–H bond angle in methane?
items.markingKey: Four bonding pairs around C: tetrahedral.

items.stem: Explain why cis- and trans- isomers of but-2-ene cannot interconvert at room temperature.
items.answer: Rotation about the C=C bond would require breaking the π bond (sideways p-orbital overlap), which needs a lot of energy.
items.markingKey: π bond restricts rotation [1]; breaking it needs much energy [1]

items.stem: Explain why the carbon chain of butane is described as zig-zag rather than straight.
items.answer: Each carbon is tetrahedral (109.5°), so successive C–C bonds are angled.
items.markingKey: tetrahedral carbons [1]; 109.5° gives zig-zag [1]

items.stem: For a molecule of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 7 σ, 1 π; sp³ (CH₃) and sp² (COOH): sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp² carbon 120°; not all atoms in one plane (sp³ carbon(s) present)
items.markingKey: σ = 7 and π = 1 [1]; angles sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp² carbon 120° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: For a molecule of propyne, CH≡CCH₃, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 6 σ, 2 π; sp (C≡C) and sp³ (CH₃): sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp carbon 180°; not all atoms in one plane (sp³ carbon(s) present)
items.markingKey: σ = 6 and π = 2 [1]; angles sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp carbon 180° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: A computational chemist in Seoul models the shape of propanone, CH₃COCH₃. (a) State the number of σ and π bonds. (b) State the hybridisation and bond angles around each carbon atom.
items.answer: (a) 9 σ and 1 π (b) sp³ (CH₃) and sp² (C=O): sp³ 109.5°, sp² 120°
items.markingKey: (a) 9 σ and 1 π [2] (b) sp³ (CH₃) and sp² (C=O): sp³ 109.5°, sp² 120° [2]

items.stem: Why is the ethene molecule planar?
options: the π bond requires the p orbitals on both carbons to be parallel, keeping all atoms in one plane
the carbon atoms are sp³ hybridised
items.answer: the π bond requires the p orbitals on both carbons to be parallel, keeping all atoms in one plane
items.markingKey: sp² carbons with π overlap.

items.stem: Kwame writes in a revision note: "In propene all the carbon atoms are trigonal planar." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Only the two C=C carbons are trigonal planar (sp², 120°); the CH₃ carbon is tetrahedral (109.5°).
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: In a test answer, Felix states: "In propene all the carbon atoms are trigonal planar." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Only the two C=C carbons are trigonal planar (sp², 120°); the CH₃ carbon is tetrahedral (109.5°).
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: For a molecule of but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 11 σ, 1 π; sp³ and sp²: sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp² carbon 120°; not all atoms in one plane (sp³ carbon(s) present)
items.markingKey: σ = 11 and π = 1 [1]; angles sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp² carbon 120° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: For a molecule of propanenitrile, CH₃CH₂CN, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 8 σ, 2 π; sp³ and sp (C≡N carbon): sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp carbon 180°; not all atoms in one plane (sp³ carbon(s) present)
items.markingKey: σ = 8 and π = 2 [1]; angles sp³ carbon 109.5°, sp carbon 180° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: Kenji studies the bonding in buta-1,3-diene, CH₂=CHCH=CH₂. (a) State the number of σ and π bonds. (b) Explain why there is restricted rotation about the double bond.
items.answer: (a) 9 σ and 2 π (b) Rotation would break the π overlap.
items.markingKey: (a) 9 σ and 2 π [2] (b) Rotation would break the π overlap. [1]

items.stem: Ravi studies the bonding in methanal, HCHO. (a) State the number of σ and π bonds. (b) Explain why there is restricted rotation about the double bond. (c) Explain why the double bond is a site of electrophilic attack.
items.answer: (a) 3 σ and 1 π (b) Rotation would break the π overlap. (c) High electron density of π electrons exposed.
items.markingKey: (a) 3 σ and 1 π [2] (b) Rotation would break the π overlap. [1] (c) High electron density of π electrons exposed. [1]

items.stem: What are structural isomers?
options: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements in space
items.answer: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
items.markingKey: Chain, positional or functional-group isomers.

items.stem: Explain why but-1-ene does not show cis/trans isomerism but but-2-ene does.
items.answer: In but-1-ene one carbon of the C=C carries two H atoms (identical groups); in but-2-ene each C=C carbon has H and CH₃.
items.markingKey: but-1-ene has two identical groups on one C [1]; but-2-ene different groups on each C [1]

items.stem: Explain why a mixture of equal amounts of two enantiomers has no effect on plane-polarised light.
items.answer: It is a racemic mixture: the equal and opposite rotations cancel out.
items.markingKey: racemic, equal amounts [1]; rotations cancel [1]

items.stem: Ethanol and methoxymethane both have the molecular formula C₂H₆O. State the type of isomerism shown and describe one chemical test that would distinguish them.
items.answer: Functional group isomerism (alcohol vs ether). Warm with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇: ethanol turns it from orange to green; methoxymethane does not (or Na: H₂ with ethanol only).
items.markingKey: functional group isomerism [1]; suitable test [1]; result for each [1]

items.stem: Propene and cyclopropane both have the molecular formula C₃H₆. State the type of isomerism shown and describe one chemical test that would distinguish them.
items.answer: Functional group isomerism (alkene vs cycloalkane). Shake with bromine water: propene decolourises it (orange to colourless); cyclopropane does not react at room temperature in the dark.
items.markingKey: functional group isomerism [1]; suitable test [1]; result for each [1]

items.stem: Propanoic acid and methyl ethanoate both have the molecular formula C₃H₆O₂. State the type of isomerism shown and describe one chemical test that would distinguish them.
items.answer: Functional group isomerism (carboxylic acid vs ester). Add sodium carbonate solution: propanoic acid effervesces (CO₂); the ester does not.
items.markingKey: functional group isomerism [1]; suitable test [1]; result for each [1]

items.stem: A flavour company in Madrid uses butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, and needs to know about its isomers. (a) Define the term stereoisomers. (b) Explain which type(s) of stereoisomerism butan-2-ol shows. (c) Explain how optical isomers can be distinguished.
items.answer: (a) Compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space. (b) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. (c) They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.
items.markingKey: (a) Compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space. [1] (b) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. [2] (c) They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions. [1]

items.stem: What is a chiral centre?
options: a carbon atom with a double bond
a carbon atom bonded to four identical groups
a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups
items.answer: a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups
items.markingKey: Gives non-superimposable mirror images (enantiomers).

items.stem: Explain why drug molecules with a chiral centre are often produced as a single enantiomer.
items.answer: Only one enantiomer may fit the biological receptor/enzyme; the other may be inactive or harmful, and separating them is costly.
items.markingKey: one enantiomer active [1]; other may be harmful/wasted [1]

items.stem: In a test answer, Hana states: "Propan-2-ol is chiral because carbon 2 has an OH group." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Carbon 2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it is not a chiral centre.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Tomás writes in a revision note: "Propan-2-ol is chiral because carbon 2 has an OH group." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Carbon 2 carries two identical CH₃ groups, so it is not a chiral centre.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A student in Lima claims that cis/trans isomers have different structural formulae. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. They have the same structural formula; the arrangement in space differs (stereoisomers).
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Deduce the number of structural isomers of C₄H₈O that are aldehydes and ketones, and name them.
items.answer: 3: butanal, 2-methylpropanal, butanone
items.markingKey: 3 isomers [1]; names correct [1]

items.stem: Deduce the number of structural isomers of C₄H₉Br that are halogenoalkanes, and name them.
items.answer: 4: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane
items.markingKey: 4 isomers [1]; names correct [1]

items.stem: A flavour company in Colombo uses but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, and needs to know about its isomers. (a) Describe how the 3D structures of the stereoisomers differ. (b) Explain why cis and trans isomers do not interconvert at room temperature.
items.answer: (a) cis: the two matching groups are on the same side of the C=C; trans: on opposite sides.  (b) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond.
items.markingKey: (a) cis: the two matching groups are on the same side of the C=C; trans: on opposite sides. [2] (b) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond. [1]

items.stem: Ethan investigates the isomers of 2-methylbutan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂OH. (a) Define the term stereoisomers. (b) Explain which type(s) of stereoisomerism 2-methylbutan-1-ol shows. (c) Describe how the 3D structures of the stereoisomers differ. (d) Name or draw one structural isomer of the compound.
items.answer: (a) Compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space. (b) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. items.answer: (a) CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ (b) C₅H₁₀O (c) C₅H₁₀O
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ [1]; (b) C₅H₁₀O [1]; (c) C₅H₁₀O [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Dhaka analyses three compounds: CH₃CHBrCH₃, CH₃COOCH₃, CH₂=CH₂. (a) Name compound A (CH₃CHBrCH₃) and identify its homologous series. (b) Name compound C (CH₂=CH₂) and identify its homologous series. (c) Draw the displayed formula of the first compound.
items.answer: (a) 2-bromopropane; halogenoalkane (b) ethene; alkene (c) All atoms and bonds of CH₃CHBrCH₃ shown.
items.markingKey: (a) 2-bromopropane; halogenoalkane [2] (b) ethene; alkene [2] (c) All atoms and bonds of CH₃CHBrCH₃ shown. [1]

items.stem: What is a nucleophile?
options: a positive ion that attacks a C=C bond
an electron-pair donor that attacks an electron-deficient carbon atom
a species with an unpaired electron
items.answer: an electron-pair donor that attacks an electron-deficient carbon atom
items.markingKey: e.g. OH⁻, CN⁻, NH₃, H₂O.

items.stem: "In homolytic fission the more electronegative atom takes both electrons." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. That is heterolytic fission; in homolytic fission each atom takes one electron.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: Cl•; Br⁻; OH⁻.
items.answer: Cl•: free radical; Br⁻: nucleophile; OH⁻: nucleophile
items.markingKey: Cl• free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] Br⁻ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] OH⁻ nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: In a college laboratory, students study free-radical substitution, electrophilic addition and nucleophilic substitution. (a) Identify the attacking species in the reaction of bromoethane with OH⁻ and explain why it attacks carbon. (b) Explain how Br₂ acts as an electrophile even though it is non-polar.
items.answer: (a) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative. (b) High electron density of C=C induces a dipole in Br₂; δ+ Br accepts electrons.
items.markingKey: (a) OH⁻ nucleophile; C δ+ because Br more electronegative. [2] (b) High electron density of C=C induces a dipole in Br₂; δ+ Br accepts electrons. [2]

items.stem: What is the bond angle around the CH₃ carbon in ethanal?
items.markingKey: the CH₃ carbon in ethanal: tetrahedral, 109.5°.

items.stem: A student in Doha predicts bond angles in organic molecules. Explain why the carbon chain of butane is described as zig-zag rather than straight.
items.answer: Each carbon is tetrahedral (109.5°), so successive C–C bonds are angled.
items.markingKey: tetrahedral carbons; 109.5° gives zig-zag [2]

items.stem: For a molecule of chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 5 σ, 1 π; sp²: sp² carbon 120°; all atoms coplanar
items.markingKey: σ = 5 and π = 1 [1]; angles sp² carbon 120° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: Noah studies the bonding in buta-1,3-diene, CH₂=CHCH=CH₂. (a) State the number of σ and π bonds. (b) State the hybridisation and bond angles around each carbon atom.
items.answer: (a) 9 σ and 2 π (b) sp²: sp² 120°
items.markingKey: (a) 9 σ and 2 π [2] (b) sp²: sp² 120° [2]

items.stem: A student in Mumbai claims that 2-methylpropene has cis and trans isomers. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. One carbon of the C=C carries two CH₃ groups, so no geometrical isomers.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Priya builds models of isomers of organic compounds. Explain why but-1-ene does not show cis/trans isomerism but but-2-ene does.
items.answer: In but-1-ene one carbon of the C=C carries two H atoms (identical groups); in but-2-ene each C=C carbon has H and CH₃.
items.markingKey: but-1-ene has two identical groups on one C; but-2-ene different groups on each C [2]

items.stem: Ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate both have the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. State the type of isomerism shown and describe one chemical test that would distinguish them.
items.answer: Functional group isomerism (carboxylic acid vs ester). Add sodium carbonate solution: ethanoic acid effervesces (CO₂); the ester does not.
items.markingKey: functional group isomerism [1]; suitable test [1]; result for each [1]

items.stem: Deduce the number of structural isomers of C₄H₁₀O that are alcohols, and name them.
items.answer: 4: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol
items.markingKey: 4 isomers [1]; names correct [1]

items.stem: A flavour company in Dubai uses 2-aminopropanoic acid, CH₃CH(NH₂)COOH, and needs to know about its isomers. (a) Explain which type(s) of stereoisomerism 2-aminopropanoic acid shows. (b) Name or draw one structural isomer of the compound.
items.answer: (a) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. (b) Any compound with the same molecular formula and different structure.
items.markingKey: (a) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. [2] (b) Any compound with the same molecular formula and different structure. [1]

items.stem: A flavour company in Jakarta uses pent-3-en-2-ol, CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH₃, and needs to know about its isomers. (a) Define the term stereoisomers. (b) Explain which type(s) of stereoisomerism pent-3-en-2-ol shows. (c) Name or draw one structural isomer of the compound. (d) Explain how optical isomers can be distinguished. (e) Explain why cis and trans isomers do not interconvert at room temperature.
items.answer: (a) Compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space. (b) cis/trans: C=C with two different groups on each C. Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. (c) Any compound with the same molecular formula and different structure. (d) They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions. (e) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond.
items.markingKey: (a) Compounds with the same structural formula but different arrangements of atoms in space. [1] (b) cis/trans: C=C with two different groups on each C. Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. [2] (c) Any compound with the same molecular formula and different structure. [1] (d) They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions. [1] (e) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond. [1]

items.stem: What is a skeletal formula?
options: a simplified formula showing the carbon skeleton as lines, with functional groups shown
a formula showing every atom and bond
a formula showing only the functional group
items.answer: a simplified formula showing the carbon skeleton as lines, with functional groups shown
items.markingKey: Each line end/junction is a C; H atoms on C not shown.

items.stem: A student in Nairobi is revising organic formulae and nomenclature. Explain why members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties.
items.answer: They contain the same functional group, which determines how the molecules react.
items.markingKey: same functional group; functional group determines reactions [2]

items.stem: Yusuf is naming organic compounds found in a fragrance laboratory in Bogotá. (a) Explain the difference between a displayed formula and a structural formula. (b) Explain why the boiling points of the alkanes increase with chain length.
items.answer: (a) A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond; a structural formula shows the arrangement of atoms in each carbon unit without showing all bonds (e.g. CH₃CH₂OH). (b) Longer molecules have more electrons and larger surface area, so stronger instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces.
items.markingKey: (a) displayed shows all bonds; structural shows groupings without bonds [2] (b) more electrons/surface contact; stronger London forces [2]

items.stem: For propan-1-ol, give (a) the structural formula, (b) the molecular formula and (c) the empirical formula.
items.answer: (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH (b) C₃H₈O (c) C₃H₈O
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH [1]; (b) C₃H₈O [1]; (c) C₃H₈O [1]

items.stem: A perfume chemist in Accra analyses three compounds: CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂COOH, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃. (a) Give the molecular formula of each compound. (b) Draw the displayed formula of the first compound.
items.answer: (a) C₄H₁₀O; C₃H₆O₂; C₄H₈O₂ (b) All atoms and bonds of CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ shown.
items.markingKey: (a) C₄H₁₀O; C₃H₆O₂; C₄H₈O₂ [2] (b) All atoms and bonds of CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ shown. [1]

items.stem: Tariq is given three compounds in a quality-control laboratory: HCHO, CH₃CH₂Br, CH₂=C(CH₃)₂. (a) Name compound B (CH₃CH₂Br) and identify its homologous series. (b) Give the molecular formula of each compound. (c) Define the term functional group.
items.answer: (a) bromoethane; halogenoalkane (b) CH₂O; BrC₂H₅; C₄H₈ (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
items.markingKey: (a) bromoethane; halogenoalkane [2] (b) CH₂O; BrC₂H₅; C₄H₈ [2] (c) An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound. [1]

items.stem: What is an electrophile?
options: an electron-pair acceptor that attacks a region of high electron density
a species with an unpaired electron
items.answer: an electron-pair acceptor that attacks a region of high electron density
items.markingKey: e.g. H⁺, Br⁺ (polarised Br₂), carbocations.

items.stem: Ravi is classifying organic reactions and reagents for an AS assignment. Explain why UV light is needed for the reaction of methane with chlorine.
items.answer: UV provides energy for homolytic fission of the Cl–Cl bond to form chlorine radicals that start the chain reaction.
items.markingKey: homolytic fission of Cl₂; radicals initiate chain [2]

items.stem: Classify each of the following as a nucleophile, an electrophile or a free radical, giving a reason in each case: H₂O; a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃; Cl•.
items.answer: H₂O: nucleophile; a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃: electrophile; Cl•: free radical
items.markingKey: H₂O nucleophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] a carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃ electrophile with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1] Cl• free radical with reason (lone pair donor / electron-pair acceptor / unpaired electron) [1]

items.stem: In a quality-control laboratory, students study free-radical substitution, electrophilic addition and nucleophilic substitution. (a) Name the mechanism of each reaction. (b) State what is shown by a curly arrow.
items.answer: (a) free-radical substitution; electrophilic addition; nucleophilic substitution (b) Movement of a pair of electrons.
items.markingKey: (a) free-radical substitution; electrophilic addition; nucleophilic substitution [3] (b) Movement of a pair of electrons. [1]

items.stem: What is the arrangement of bonds around the carbon of the COOH group in ethanoic acid?
items.answer: trigonal planar
items.markingKey: trigonal planar (120°).

items.stem: "In propene all the carbon atoms are trigonal planar." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Only the two C=C carbons are trigonal planar (sp², 120°); the CH₃ carbon is tetrahedral (109.5°).
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: For a molecule of ethane, C₂H₆, state the number of σ and π bonds and the bond angles around each type of carbon atom. Explain whether all the atoms lie in one plane.
items.answer: 7 σ, 0 π; sp³: sp³ carbon 109.5°; not all atoms in one plane (sp³ carbon(s) present)
items.markingKey: σ = 7 and π = 0 [1]; angles sp³ carbon 109.5° [1]; planarity explained [1]

items.stem: Isla studies the bonding in ethanal, CH₃CHO. (a) State the number of σ and π bonds. (b) State the hybridisation and bond angles around each carbon atom.
items.answer: (a) 6 σ and 1 π (b) sp³ (CH₃) and sp² (CHO): sp³ 109.5°, sp² 120°
items.markingKey: (a) 6 σ and 1 π [2] (b) sp³ (CH₃) and sp² (CHO): sp³ 109.5°, sp² 120° [2]

items.stem: Mei builds models of isomers of organic compounds. Explain why a mixture of equal amounts of two enantiomers has no effect on plane-polarised light.
items.answer: It is a racemic mixture: the equal and opposite rotations cancel out.
items.markingKey: racemic, equal amounts; rotations cancel [2]

items.stem: Explain whether 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, shows stereoisomerism.
items.answer: Yes: it has a chiral carbon bonded to four different groups, so it exists as two non-superimposable mirror images.
items.markingKey: correct conclusion [1]; structural reason [1]

items.stem: Deduce the number of structural isomers of C₅H₁₀O that are aldehydes and ketones, and name them.
items.answer: 7: pentanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, 2,2-dimethylpropanal, pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one, 3-methylbutan-2-one
items.markingKey: 7 isomers [1]; names correct [1]

items.stem: Deduce the number of structural isomers of C₄H₈O₂ that are esters, and name them.
items.answer: 4: methyl propanoate, ethyl ethanoate, propyl methanoate, 1-methylethyl methanoate
items.markingKey: 4 isomers [1]; names correct [1]

items.stem: Ethan investigates the isomers of but-2-enoic acid, CH₃CH=CHCOOH. (a) Describe how the 3D structures of the stereoisomers differ. (b) Explain why cis and trans isomers do not interconvert at room temperature.
items.answer: (a) cis: the two matching groups are on the same side of the C=C; trans: on opposite sides.  (b) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond.
items.markingKey: (a) cis: the two matching groups are on the same side of the C=C; trans: on opposite sides. [2] (b) The π bond prevents rotation about the C=C bond. [1]

items.stem: Tomás investigates the isomers of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, CH₃CH(OH)COOH. (a) Explain which type(s) of stereoisomerism 2-hydroxypropanoic acid shows. (b) Describe how the 3D structures of the stereoisomers differ. (c) Name or draw one structural isomer of the compound. (d) Explain how optical isomers can be distinguished.
items.answer: (a) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. (b) Two tetrahedral arrangements about the chiral carbon that are non-superimposable mirror images. (c) Any compound with the same molecular formula and different structure. (d) They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.
items.markingKey: (a) Optical: chiral carbon with four different groups. [2] (b) Two tetrahedral arrangements about the chiral carbon that are non-superimposable mirror images.
